preamble: Gliding of the alveolar tap [ɾ] to a palatal glide [j]/[i̯] in syllable-final position. The best-documented case is the Cibaeño Spanish of the northern Dominican Republic, where coda /ɾ/ (and /l/) is vocalized to a front glide, so that correr is heard as correi and perdón as peidón.

examples.note: Syllable-final /ɾ/ is replaced by a front glide in the northern Cibao region.
Word-internal coda /ɾ/ vocalized; final /l/ merges into the same glide in El Cibao and El Seibo.
